Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Parallel Computer Architecture [NPT_4132]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Explain how architectural scalability is influenced by interconnection network topology in parallel     (5)  
  systems. Compare mesh and fat-tree architectures in terms of latency and bandwidth utilization  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Evaluate the effectiveness of shared-memory versus message-passing models for parallel                  (5)  
  programming. Under what workload conditions does one outperform the other?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Evaluate how virtual memory design influences parallel program scalability. Apply the different         (5)  
  strategies to reduce TLB and page-fault overheads in high-core-count systems  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)           Explain how snooping and directory-based cache coherence protocols handle write operations              (5)  
  differently. Illustrate the trade-off between scalability and coherence traffic in both approaches.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
3)                Evaluate the effectiveness of the MESI and Dragon protocols for a multicore processor with high         (5)  
  write-sharing workloads. Which protocol offers better performance and why?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Propose an improved coherence strategy for a system using multi-level caches with an atomic bus. (5)  
  Justify your design choices with respect to latency, bandwidth, and consistency guarantees  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)                Analyze how integrating a split-transaction bus affects cache miss handling and bus arbitration in      (5)  
  multi-level cache hierarchies. Discuss its impact on fairness and ordering.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Assess the correctness conditions (write serialization, data consistency, and absence of live lock)     (5)  
  for a cache-based directory protocol. How do these properties ensure reliable shared-memory  
  execution?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  Page #1

5)                        Evaluate barrier synchronization techniques in shared-memory multiprocessors. How do hardware- (5)  
  based and software-based barriers differ in terms of latency and scalability?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)                Evaluate deterministic and adaptive routing strategies in interconnection networks. Propose a       (5)  
  hybrid routing mechanism that minimizes deadlock while optimizing throughput.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  -----End-----
